items.item:
12. Two concurrent creates with one request id and equal facts — of a
    project, a Customer, a room of one project, a pointer of one project by
    one publisher (for Kernel, naming one session) — make one record; the
    other answers it. With different facts, or another publisher, the second
    is refused as a conflict. The same request id for rooms of two different
    projects makes two rooms.
   Shows A01-1, A01-3, A01-4. [witness: verification:registry_a01_concurrent_creates_make_one_record]
statements:
```text
for each model m in {Project, Customer}, and per project for m in
{Room, ArtifactPointer}: records r1 != r2 of m with request ids present have
r1.request_id != r2.request_id   -- A01-1
create(m, request_id = k, facts = f), an existing r of m holding k, and a
check of stages (1) to (4) of A04 rule 6 fails => refused, store unchanged   -- A01-2
create(m, request_id = k, facts = f) with m in {Room, ArtifactPointer}, an
existing r of m holding k, stages (1) to (4) passed, and its project
archived => refused, store unchanged   -- A01-5
create(m, request_id = k, facts = f), an existing r of m holding k, stages
(1) to (4) passed, for m in {Room, ArtifactPointer} its project not
archived, and f = current_facts(r) => answer r, store unchanged   -- A01-3
create(m, request_id = k, facts = f), an existing r of m holding k, stages
(1) to (4) passed, for m in {Room, ArtifactPointer} its project not
archived, and f != current_facts(r) => refused, store unchanged   -- A01-4
```

verdicts.why: The check races equal and unequal creates for projects, customers, project-scoped rooms, and project-and-publisher-scoped pointers, verifying one stored record plus an unchanged repeat or one accepted create plus a conflict. It also verifies that the same room request ID is independent across projects and that changing the pointer publisher, including the Kernel session, is refused without changing the store.
